version.changelog:
Initial release of the App Store API skill.

- Provides Apple App Store API alternative with pay-per-call (USDC/x402) or prepaid credits.
- Supports searching apps/bundles, fetching full details, reviews (by recent/helpful), similar apps, and developer catalogs across any country storefront.
- No Apple Developer Program membership required; no storefront scraping.
- All endpoints are HTTP GET and require only the necessary parameters.
- Example curl commands and error codes included for easy integration.

llm.summary: This skill is a straightforward paid Apple App Store data API guide with the cost and authentication model disclosed.

dimensions.detail: Network access to appstore.fetcher.sh and optional API credentials are proportionate to the API-client purpose; it does not request local file, system, browser profile, or broad environment access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is Markdown documentation only, with no bundled executable scripts, package install commands, hooks, or local code execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs use of a fetcher.sh API, bearer-key authentication, x402 payment flow, and an MCP server; this is scoped to App Store data access, though repeated calls can incur charges.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, privilege escalation, background worker, memory modification, or tool hijacking behavior appears in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is App Store search, details, reviews, similar apps, bundles, and developer catalog lookup, and the artifact only documents GET endpoints for that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use a paid fetcher.sh App Store API. Confirm before repeated or automated calls, protect any FETCHER_API_KEY like a payment credential, and understand that x402 or prepaid-credit use may spend funds even though each listed call is low cost.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The finding concerns paid API usage. The artifact discloses pay-per-call/prepaid usage in the description and early text and lists $0.003 per GET endpoint, so this is a user-awareness note rather than a security concern.
